newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges firm a bit with tighter supply.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges firm a bit with tighter supply.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barge prices firmed a little in a quiet market at the start of the week, with two majors reported having problems with loadings, traders said.

High sulphur barges were traded at $94 and $94.25 a tonne fob in Rotterdam with a major said to be the buyer and offers rose to $95 later, while RMG material was heard done at $93 in the Antwerp area. Friday's trade range was $92.50 to $93.50.
"Some people are having problems with loadings so there is a little bit of a shortage," one trader said.

"Antwerp is calm today and there's only one player in Rotterdam looking for products...Bunker enquiries are calm but may pick up. We may see a price increase in both Rotterdam and Antwerp later in the day," a second trader said.

Traders were mixed over high sulphur cracked cargoes, with some assessing them around the $88/$89 mark with little good quality material available while others, arguing supplies were available, assessed cargoes a few dollars lower.
One trader dismissed reports of a shortage of supply saying that he will have seven cargoes coming in soon with a price tag of about two means plus $1.50.
Low sulphur barges were quietly offered at $97, or unchanged from Friday, and buyers were $2 lower but no trades were heard in that market.
